name: atrial fibrillation overview
title: Atrial fibrillation decision chart: each of its three harms has its own treatment; stroke risk scored by CHADS2 decides anticoagulation, a fast ventricular rate gets AV-nodal blocking drugs, and lost atrial kick gets rhythm control, with cardioversion now only if onset is under 48 hours or the patient is already anticoagulated, otherwise after 3 weeks of anticoagulation

root.title: Atrial fibrillation (AF): irregularly irregular, no P waves. Treat EACH of its three harms
lines: fibrillatory baseline waves, irregular RR intervals · risk rises after 50
look for a reversible cause: hypertension, ischemic or valve disease, alcohol, thyroid, lung disease, sleep apnea
PAROXYSMAL stops on its own · PERSISTENT needs drugs or cardioversion · PERMANENT: rate control only

groups.title: 1 · STROKE
lines: blood stagnates in a big left atrium and clots

groups.title: 3 · LOST atrial kick
lines: less left ventricular filling, less cardiac output

head: h
ANTICOAGULATE
for every patient with a risk factor
clue: • Congestive heart failure, Hypertension, Age > 75, Diabetes: 1 each
• prior Stroke or transient ischemic attack: 2
~mitral stenosis is a very high risk too
tx: e.g. apixaban 5 mg twice daily, or warfarin

head: h
RATE CONTROL
the AV node lets the ventricles race
clue: ~AF can also run normal or slow: then no slowing needed

head: h
RHYTHM CONTROL
a judgement call: young, symptomatic, recent onset
never in PERMANENT AF
clue: How long has it been in AF?
a clot can form in the atrial appendage after 48 h
